content_of_post_to_comment:
Recently I was wondering if I was just bad at focusing.

I’d sit down to work, open my laptop and tell myself I will start in a minute. Then I’d check one message, open another tab, pick up my phone, maybe look up something completely unrelated. Nothing major just little things.

Then I’d look at the time and 20 minutes were gone. Sometimes more. And I hadn’t even properly started.

This happened so often that I started trying to fix my productivity. Better to-do lists, timers, different ways of planning my day. Some of it helped for a while but I’d eventually end up doing the same thing again.

At some point I started noticing what I was doing right before I actually started working. Most days I was sitting down with my phone right next to me, notifications on, tabs already open and no real idea what I was going to do first. Then I’d get distracted and blame my focus.

Now I spend like 10 minutes before I start just getting things out of the way. I close tabs I don’t need, open whatever I am actually working on and put my phone somewhere I’d have to get up to reach. Sometimes I will just sit there for a minute because I am usually in such a rush to start doing something that I end up doing nothing.

It’s pretty basic lol, but it’s helped more than I expected. I still get distracted. I still check my phone sometimes. But if I can get through those first 10-15 minutes without messing around, I usually settle into the work a lot easier.

Does anyone else do something like this before starting work?
comment: I’ve noticed the same thing with my own work sessions: a lot of “focus problems” are really “too many easy exits available” problems. The phone across the room part is underrated because it adds a tiny bit of friction before the impulse turns into a 20-minute detour. I’ve also found deciding the very first task before sitting down helps a lot, because vague starts are where distractions sneak in.
